scope.artifact_limit: No APK/XAPK bytes were downloaded or inspected in this research run; no signer comparison was performed. Listing metadata is not artifact evidence.

decision_rule: A public listing with an explicit package match is enough to mark a metadata mapping candidate, but not enough to enable a production source fallback. Enablement remains NO until the selected version's downloaded artifact is checked for package, version, SDK/ABI suitability, and signer/hash evidence against an accepted source.

global_findings: The eight missing cross-store mappings are exactly YouTube, AdGuard, Google Photos, Truecaller, Instagram, Reddit, Edge, and Key Mapper when comparing targets.json source choices with apps.json store keys.

Seven of those eight have a public alternate listing whose page/search evidence explicitly names the target package: YouTube, Photos, Truecaller on APKPure; Instagram, Reddit, Edge, Key Mapper on APKMirror. AdGuard has no verified APKPure page; its official APK page and APKMirror exact package are available.

No target can be marked enable-now from listing metadata alone in this run. Source_download.sh ultimately produces an APK/XAPK that still needs artifact_identity and SDK/ABI checks; this research did not obtain bytes or signers.

APKMirror pages sometimes publish min SDK/ABI and abbreviated signature fingerprints, but those are page claims about a remote artifact and are not a substitute for local bytes/signature verification.
MX Player Pro is a paid Play app. Search results for APKPure identified free MX Player (com.mxtech.videoplayer.ad), not the Pro package; that is not a valid fallback for com.mxtech.videoplayer.pro.
